name: Forms
job: Every form outside people fill in, on your site, in Google Forms or from an ad, each answer sent to the work it belongs to
intro: Answers from your website forms, Google Forms and Meta lead ads land in one queue with a clock on each. The Lemma reads what each one is and sends it to the right person, with the reason. A reply is drafted in their mailbox, and nothing goes until they press Send.
does: Every answer in one queue, not sure first, then by how long it has waited, with spam set aside and one key to put it back.
Sent to one person with the reason: an open deal's owner first, then your rules, then the form's owner. Bugs can go to Triage.
A reply drafted in the owner's own mailbox, a line in their Today, and the honest time to first reply.

accounts.why: Through Mail: each person connects their own mailbox, so the reply to an answer is drafted there and sent when they press Send.
Reads new answers to the Google Forms you add, every 15 minutes, from the account of whoever added them.
Reads new leads from the lead forms you pick, every 15 minutes. Not checked against a live account yet.

setup: Once for the whole Lemma: tick where people fill in forms for you, and turn on a website form (Contact us is on by default). Share its link, put it on your page, or in your product.
Say who gets what, or skip it and everything goes to you. Or look around with a sample week first.
Each person opens Forms once, so answers sent to them reach their Today, and connects their mail for drafted replies.

hero.sub: Website forms, Google Forms and ad leads in one queue. Each one is read, sent to whoever should reply, and the reply is drafted before they open it.

steps.title: Turn on a form and share it.
steps.body: Start with Contact us: a link, a form on your own page, or inside your product. Add Google Forms by pasting its edit link.

steps.title: Say who gets what.
steps.body: An open deal's owner first, then your rules, then each form's owner. Skip it and everything comes to you.

steps.title: Reply from a draft.
steps.body: The owner finds the reply already written in their own mailbox and in their Today. They read it, then send.

moments.label: Speed
moments.title: A reply drafted three minutes in.
moments.body: The answer is read, sent to its owner and answered in a draft in their own mailbox, while the person who wrote is still at their desk.

moments.label: Who gets it
moments.title: Sent to the right person, with why.
moments.body: When their company already has an open deal, its owner gets it. Every rule it checked is shown, marked used or not needed.

moments.label: Bugs
moments.title: A bug through Contact us goes to Triage.
moments.body: Someone reports a fault on your contact form. It becomes an item in Triage, and the answer shows its number and owner.

moments.label: Every door
moments.title: Every door on one page.
moments.body: Website forms, Google Forms, ad lead forms and other plugins' forms, each with its count, its rule and whether it is still taking answers.

moments.label: Who they are
moments.title: Who they are, beside what they wrote.
moments.body: Their People map card, their company and its open deal sit next to the answer, so the reply starts from what the team already knows.

moments.label: Spam
moments.title: Spam is one key, and so is undo.
moments.body: S sets a pitch aside with the reason, never deleted. U puts it back, and each correction teaches the next read.

trust.title: Nothing sends on its own.
trust.body: Every reply is a draft in the owner's mailbox until they press Send. The chat beside a form answers only from what you've published.

trust.title: Spam set aside, never deleted.
trust.body: Every answer is kept, with the reason it was set aside, and one key puts it back.

trust.title: What they wrote is the team's.
trust.body: An answer to a team form is readable by everyone in the Lemma. Leave Careers off if applications should stay private.

faq.a: Its own website forms, Google Forms and Meta lead ads. Typeform, Tally, Webflow, Fillout, Google Ads and LinkedIn through Zapier come once your Lemma has a webhook address.

faq.q: Does it ever reply on its own?
faq.a: No. A reply is drafted in the owner's mailbox and goes only when they press Send.

faq.q: What if it isn't sure where an answer goes?
faq.a: It asks the form's owner to pick. After an hour with no pick, it goes to them anyway, still marked not sure.

faq.q: Can I change the form's fields?
faq.a: Rename, switch off or add fields on each form. The form's link shows the form's own name for now; your own page can set its title and thank-you.

closing: Answer every form while they're still waiting.
